## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

turns.reply:
The ANSI parser now strips the private Fp escape sequences `\x1b0`–`\x1b?`, including the cursor save/restore codes `\x1b7` and `\x1b8`. The change is one regex alternative in `rich/ansi.py`.

I checked it with `Text.from_ansi`: `'a\x1b7b\x1b8c\x1b[1mBold\x1b[0m'` gives `'abcBold'` with bold applied, and `'x\x1b0y\x1b?z'` gives `'xyz'`. `tests/test_ansi.py` passes (7 tests).

The issue also asks for a CHANGELOG entry, which I did not add. I'll submit the patch now.

The ANSI parser in `rich/ansi.py` now matches the private Fp escape sequences `\x1b0`–`\x1b?` and drops them, so `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` no longer leak into output. The patch is submitted (1 file, 335 bytes). I checked it with `Text.from_ansi` and `tests/test_ansi.py` (7 passed), but I did not add a new test or the CHANGELOG entry the issue mentions.
